acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Agadir is one of the safest cities in Morocco for tourists. It's a modern, purpose-built resort city with excellent infrastructure. Crime against tourists is rare, and locals are genuinely welcoming to families with children. Standard precautions apply (watch belongings, supervise kids in crowds).

mainEntity.name: What's the best age to take kids to Agadir?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agadir works for all ages, but each stage has its sweet spot. Toddlers (1-3) enjoy the beach and gentle activities. Ages 4-8 get the most from Crocoparc, camel rides, and Paradise Valley. Pre-teens and teenagers love the adventure activities and cultural experiences. Babies are welcome everywhere—Moroccans adore children!

mainEntity.name: Are Agadir beaches safe for children?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Agadir Bay is one of the safest beaches in Morocco for children. The bay is protected from strong currents and large waves. Water is shallow near shore with gradual depth increase. Lifeguards patrol during peak hours. Always supervise children and avoid swimming during rough weather.

mainEntity.name: What should kids wear in Agadir?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casual, comfortable clothing is fine everywhere in Agadir. For beach: swimwear, hats, and cover-ups. For excursions: comfortable shoes, light layers, sun protection. Agadir is more relaxed about dress code than other Moroccan cities, but covering shoulders and knees is respectful when visiting local markets or villages.

mainEntity.name: Is Moroccan food suitable for children?

acceptedAnswer.text: Generally yes! Tagine (slow-cooked stew) and couscous are mild and flavorful. Grilled meats and chicken are widely available. Fresh bread is delicious. For picky eaters, French fries, pizza, and pasta are available in tourist areas. Avoid very spicy dishes and street food salads with young children.

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget for family activities in Agadir?

acceptedAnswer.text: Budget €50-100 per day for a family of four for activities and excursions. Many experiences (beach, Kasbah viewpoint, exploring the souk) are free. Paid activities range from €15 (camel ride) to €60 (cooking class). Tours like Paradise Valley (€25-35pp) include transport, guide, and lunch—good value for families.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book activities in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: For popular activities during peak season (December-February, July-August), booking 1-2 days ahead is recommended. Activities like cooking classes and specialty tours should be booked in advance. Beach activities, Crocoparc, and market visits don't require booking.

mainEntity.name: Is there a kids' club or childcare available in Agadir?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many resort hotels offer kids' clubs and babysitting services. Check with your specific hotel. Some beach clubs also offer supervised activities for children. For serious childcare needs, book a hotel with dedicated kids' facilities.
